findings.title: update() judges the 'before' state with the org-aware wrapper, so login-cache invalidation is skipped for IDPs of disabled orgs
findings.body: update() gets idpById via getById(), which returns the organization-aware wrapper from createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel. That wrapper's isEnabled() returns false whenever the owning organization is disabled. So when the org is disabled, getLoginPredicate().test(original) is false even though the IDP is raw-enabled and its id is in the cached ORG_ONLY/ALL login lists (the DB query does not check org enablement). If the update then also makes the IDP non-login (hideOnLogin=true, linkOnly, BROKER_PUBLIC=false, or enabled=false), both predicates are false and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate returns without invalidating. When the org is later re-enabled, getForLogin returns the stale entry; the wrapper now reports enabled, and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled(), so a hidden or link-only IDP is shown on the login page. remove() avoids this by using the raw idpDelegate.getByAlias(), so the 'original' state should likewise come from the raw model (e.g. idpDelegate.getById) rather than the wrapped getById().

findings.title: Cleanup removes an IDP named literally 'alias' instead of the IDPs created in the loop
findings.body: The cleanup registers testRealm().identityProviders().get('alias')::remove, which targets a nonexistent provider with the literal alias 'alias', so the 'idp-alias-N' providers created in the loop are never removed (the same mistake is repeated at line 425 for 'idp-alias-20'). The leftover IDPs stay linked to the organization and can leak into other tests in the class or leave the cleanup itself failing with a 404. The cleanup should capture the actual alias in a final local and call get(thatAlias)::remove.

findings.title: testCacheIDPForLogin never checks that creating or removing a login-eligible IDP invalidates the login caches
findings.body: Step 1 only creates a hidden IDP and removes a disabled IDP, and asserts that the caches survive. Neither operation qualifies for login, so the registerIDPLoginInvalidation calls in create() and remove() are never shown to invalidate anything. A regression that drops those calls would pass this test. The test also has no scenario where the owning organization is disabled, which is the case where the wrapper changes login eligibility and where update() currently skips invalidation incorrectly. Add steps that create and remove a login-eligible IDP, and one that changes a linked IDP's login status while its org is disabled.

findings.title: getForLogin Javadoc omits the new requirement that org-linked IDPs must be public
findings.body: The Javadoc says an IDP can be used for login if it is enabled, not link-only, and not hidden on login. The PR adds to getLoginPredicate a rule that IDPs bound to an organization must have BROKER_PUBLIC=true, and the ORG_ONLY query filters on the same flag. Neither this Javadoc nor the LoginFilter enum documentation mentions it, so SPI implementers and callers reading the contract will not know that org-bound IDPs need the public flag to be listed for login.

findings.title: Cache search key maps null and empty organizationId to the same entry, although the underlying queries differ
findings.body: searchKey is computed as organizationId != null ? organizationId : "". The default getForLogin only adds the ORGANIZATION_ID criterion when organizationId is non-null, so a null argument (all organizations) and an empty-string argument (criterion applied with an empty value) are different queries. Both are cached under the same cacheKey and searchKey, so a call with one value can return the cached result of the other, depending on call order. No current caller passes an empty string, so the impact is latent, but the key construction is ambiguous. Use a distinct sentinel for the null case.
